title: Tech Note: How to Save and Restore 4D Hierarchical Lists
author: Charles “Charlie” Vass, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: 4D Hierarchical Lists (in-memory ListRef objects and form-level list objects)
BLOB to list / list to BLOB commands
On Backup Startup/Shutdown Database Method hooks
Recursive method design for nested list structures

historical_commentary.text: This note addressed a real pain point of the classic Design-mode era: hierarchical lists were stored inside the binary structure (.4DB) file, so any user customization to a list was silently lost whenever a developer redeployed a new structure, forcing developers to build custom XML/BLOB export-import archiving around backups. The underlying problem is substantially reduced today because 4D's Project mode (text-based .4DProject) makes structure elements diffable and versionable, and many list-like configuration needs are now more naturally modeled with ORDA entities or JSON preferences rather than binary hierarchical list objects, though the classic List/ListRef commands themselves still exist and function for backward compatibility.
related_updates: Project mode (4D v17+, 2018) stores structure elements as text, reducing (though not eliminating) the class of "lost user customization on redeploy" problems this note solves for hierarchical lists

Storing user-configurable list-like data in a JSON preferences file or an ORDA-backed table is now often preferred over binary Hierarchical List objects for this kind of persisted, user-editable configuration
The 4D SAX XML and List/ListRef commands used in this note remain functional and backward compatible in current 4D versions
